research_questions: Which channel is suppressed: pain experience, touch or pressure, proprioception, sight, hearing, smell or taste, or a declared multimodal combination?
Who causes the suppression: the subject, another caster, an environmental trap, or an artifact?
Is the intended phase activation, maintained information asymmetry, release, or delayed recognition?
What visible evidence distinguishes an awake subject attending elsewhere from hypnosis, sleep, paralysis, or stopped time?
Can one composition establish the subject, suppression boundary, simultaneous hidden event, and consequence, or is a sequence required?
Which claims are request metadata because a still image cannot establish subjective sensation or awareness?

intent_boundaries.core_intent: An awake subject continues a visible activity while one or more explicitly selected sensory channels are fictionally suppressed, creating a contrast between the subject's displayed attention and a simultaneous event outside the available information channel.
included: channel-selective suppression with an explicit affected body region
self-cast, other-cast, trap-triggered, and artifact-mediated variants
single-frame split-level or cutaway staging of simultaneous information
two- or three-phase activation, hidden event, and release or recognition sequences
calm, distracted, suspicious, or post-release visible reactions as presentation choices
distinct_concepts: Blindfolds and ear protection physically occlude channels but do not by themselves establish magic or loss of all sensation.
Analgesia or absence of reported pain is not equivalent to loss of touch, proprioception, sight, or hearing.
Hypnosis changes attention or response under a different fictional mechanism; time stop removes simultaneity for the stopped subject; sleep removes the awake-state contrast.
A calm face shows a displayed expression, not the subject's internal awareness, pain state, or knowledge.
The phrase is attested in contemporary creator titles and fan discussion, but the available sources do not establish a stable, standardized genre taxonomy.
term_limits: The origin record uses broad language equivalent to all senses while also showing continued visual interaction; implementation must therefore ask for or infer a narrower channel scope from explicit cues instead of treating all senses as one default.
Pain, nociception, somatic touch, and proprioception are separate fields and must not be collapsed into a single factual sensory switch.
The historical-popularity claim in the origin blog is not independently verified and must not control candidate selection.

source_claims.limitation: A work title establishes occurrence, not a fixed genre definition or general popularity beyond that ranking.

source_claims.title: Touching a Rubber Hand: Feeling of Body Ownership Is Associated with Activity in Multisensory Brain Areas
source_claims.claim: In blindfolded participants, synchronized tactile and proprioceptive signals produced a somatic rubber-hand illusion, supporting that body ownership can depend on congruent multisensory integration rather than vision alone.
source_claims.limitation: The experiment does not establish magic, total sensory loss, or unawareness of unrelated events.

source_claims.title: Visual proprioception in the timing of movements: evidence from deafferentation
source_claims.claim: Two participants with severe somatosensory deafferentation relied strongly on visual feedback for movement timing; performance worsened when visual access to the movement was reduced.
source_claims.limitation: The sample is two rare clinical cases and supports a mechanistic boundary, not a universal pose rule.

source_claims.title: IASP Terminology
source_claims.claim: IASP defines pain as a personal sensory and emotional experience and nociception as neural encoding of noxious stimuli, explicitly stating that pain and nociception are different phenomena.
source_claims.limitation: The terminology separates factual concepts; it does not prescribe a fictional magic system.

source_claims.title: Visual Narrative Structure
source_claims.claim: Panels can window selected conceptual information, and separate images can depict facets of a broader environment at the same time; sequential structure also supports event and consequence inference.
source_claims.limitation: The paper supports visual-narrative organization, not the specific cutaway design or sensory-suppression trope.

factual_baseline.claim: Body ownership and movement feedback are multisensory and channel-dependent.
Pain and nociception are not interchangeable with touch, proprioception, or every other sensory modality.
Visual layouts can present simultaneous facets or ordered phases while omitting information from a panel.

fantasy_departures: A magic field can switch a selected subjective channel on or off instantly and visibly.
The subject may retain alertness and precise motor control despite declared broad sensory loss.
The viewer may see a hidden simultaneous event through a literalized cutaway unavailable to the character.
Field release can produce immediate, author-defined recognition without a factual physiological model.
design_inferences: Use channel-specific glyphs or field geometry to make the requested fictional rule legible; this is a visual convention inferred from the design problem.
Treat a visible safe task plus a separate event and non-response as evidence of attention contrast, not proof of subjective unawareness.
Prefer a local somatic or pain-channel variant when the scene also requires ordinary seeing, hearing, or precise task performance.
Use a sequence when release, duration, accumulation, or delayed recognition is material to the request.

research_questions: Is the requested material saturated sand, living quicksand with a fragile crust, a creek-bed deposit, generic mud, or a declared fantasy bog?
Which stage matters: initial crust failure, partial penetration, immobilized entrapment, self-extraction effort, assisted extraction, or aftermath?
Which surface and grain cues distinguish quicksand from opaque water, ordinary mud, or dry dune sand?
How deep is the visible interface, and is that depth factualized or intentionally cinematic?
Does one frame need only establish current entrapment, or must a sequence establish progressive sinking or rescue outcome?
Which pose, camera, and prop relations make the material response and action chain legible?

intent_boundaries.core_intent: A subject is partially entrapped in a saturated or otherwise explicitly fictional granular medium whose disturbed surface, collapsed structure, and resistance are visible through the body-material interaction.
included: initial crust break and local collapse
knee-, thigh-, or waist-level partial entrapment
helper, rope, branch, or firm-edge assisted tension chains
single-frame peril, comic mishap, adventure tension, or explanatory cutaway
multi-frame onset, worsening stage, rescue contact, or aftermath
distinct_concepts: Quicksand is not synonymous with every swamp, bog, mud pool, or body of water.
The fragile cyanobacteria-cemented crust described for living quicksand is a specific natural subtype, not a universal quicksand surface.
Swimming and treading-water poses describe a fluid body, while quicksand entrapment requires a granular interface and resisted limbs.
One still can establish current depth and struggle but cannot prove continued descent, inevitability, duration, or rescue success.
Complete cinematic engulfment is a fantasy departure from the cited salt-lake quicksand experiment for a human-density body.
term_limits: The Korean origin record groups 유사, 늪, and 수렁 as a broad peril motif; the physical material subtype must remain a separate implementation field.
A cracked surface is selected only for living-crust or explicitly brittle-surface variants.
A high-submersion fantasy variant must be labeled as a cinematic material rule rather than presented as the measured behavior of salt-lake quicksand.

source_claims.limitation: The high confidence concerns what the page says about its own uncertainty, not confidence in its genre generalizations.

source_claims.title: Liquefaction of quicksand under stress
source_claims.claim: Laboratory salt-lake quicksand became unstable under forced movement, first liquefying and then collapsing, which explains why a disturbed local surface and collapse trace are stronger cues than a flat mud plane.
source_claims.limitation: The measured material and test conditions do not define every natural or fictional quicksand.

source_claims.title: Liquefaction of quicksand under stress
source_claims.claim: The sinking test found that a human-density body could not be drawn completely into the tested salt-lake quicksand, establishing partial entrapment as the factualized default for that material.
source_claims.limitation: This does not rule on every natural basin, other hazards, or deliberately cinematic fantasy media.

source_claims.title: Living quicksand
source_claims.claim: A field study in Lençóis Maranhenses found a specific living-quicksand condition where cyanobacteria cemented an impermeable crust over a grain suspension and critical pressure caused crust failure and water release.
source_claims.limitation: This crust is a subtype-specific mechanism and must not be generalized to all quicksand.

source_claims.title: Living quicksand
source_claims.claim: After collapse, sedimentation and a rapid increase of shear strength could trap an intruder, and the studied condition did not restore itself once collapsed.
source_claims.limitation: The result applies to the studied living-quicksand system rather than every saturated granular medium.

source_claims.title: Quicksand Two Day Rescue during Winter Storms at Zion National Park
source_claims.claim: A documented 2019 incident involved one leg trapped to the knee in creek-bed quicksand and an unsuccessful self-release before a prolonged assisted extraction, showing that shallow-looking partial entrapment can still be substantial.
source_claims.limitation: A single incident validates possibility, not a universal depth, pose, or extraction sequence.

factual_baseline.claim: Disturbed saturated granular material can liquefy and collapse locally, then resist extraction as it settles.
Partial rather than complete submersion is the supported human-density outcome in the cited salt-lake experiment.
A fragile biologically cemented crust is documented for a specific living-quicksand subtype.
Real partial leg entrapment requiring assisted extraction has been officially documented.

fantasy_departures: A human-density subject continues descending until fully engulfed in a cinematic medium.
Generic swamp mud, magical mire, and salt-lake quicksand share one invented material law.
The subsurface is shown through a transparent cutaway unavailable to an in-world camera.
Depth, suction, settling speed, and release can be authored independently of measured granular rheology.
design_inferences: Use the collapsed depression, displaced wet grains, adhesion, and a clear interface as the minimum material-readable cluster.
Use a cracked thin crust only when the living-crust subtype or brittle-surface cue is selected.
Use knee-, thigh-, or waist-level partial entrapment for a factualized still; mark higher engulfment as cinematic fantasy.
Use a sequence when progressive sinking, repeated effort, or completed extraction is part of the requested claim.
Bind any helper or prop to a visible tension chain and material consequence instead of relying on proximity alone.
